title.en: Volume 59 Biographies 40: Other Peoples from Henan, the Di People, and Qiang
title.raw: 卷五十九 列傳第四十 芮芮虜 河南 氐 羌 Volume 59 Biographies 40: Other Peoples from Henan, the Di People, and Qiang

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷第五十九 列傳第四十

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 59, Biographies 40
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 59, Biographies 40

sentences.zh: 芮芮虏 河南 氐 羌

translations.literal: Rouran Barbarians; Henan; Di; Qiang
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran Barbarians; Henan; the Di; the Qiang

sentences.zh: 芮芮虜，塞外雜胡也。

translations.literal: The Rouran barbarians were miscellaneous Hu beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran were a mixed Hu people living beyond the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 編髮左衽。

translations.literal: They braided their hair and wore the lapel on the left.
translations.idiomatic: They wore braided hair and left-lapped robes.

sentences.zh: 晉世什翼圭入塞內後，芮芮逐水草，盡有匈奴故庭，威服西域。

translations.literal: In the Jin era, after Shiyijian entered within the passes, the Rouran followed water and pasture, wholly possessed the former Xiongnu court, and awed and subjugated the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: After Shiyijian of the Jin entered the interior in the Jin period, the Rouran followed pasture and water, took over the old Xiongnu heartland in full, and brought the Western Regions under their sway.

sentences.zh: 土氣早寒，所居爲穹廬氈帳。

translations.literal: The soil and air were early cold; where they dwelt were dome huts and felt tents.
translations.idiomatic: The climate turned cold early, and they lived in domed felt tents.

sentences.zh: 刻木記事，不識文書。

translations.literal: They carved wood to record affairs and did not know documents.
translations.idiomatic: They kept records by carving wood and had no knowledge of writing.

sentences.zh: 馬畜丁肥，種衆殷盛。

translations.literal: Horses and livestock were plump; the race was abundant and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Their horses and herds grew fat, and their people were numerous and thriving.

sentences.zh: 常與魏虜爲讎敵。

translations.literal: They were constantly enemies with the Wei barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: They were perennial foes of the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 二年、三年，芮芮主頻遣使貢獻貂皮雜物。

translations.literal: In the second and third years, the Rouran lord frequently sent envoys to present tribute of sable furs and miscellaneous goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the second and third years of the dynasty, the Rouran ruler repeatedly sent envoys bearing sable pelts and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 與上書欲伐魏虜，謂上「足下」，自稱「吾」。

translations.literal: In his letter to the emperor he wished to attack the Wei barbarians; he addressed the emperor as "Your Foot" and called himself "I."
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial to the throne he proposed attacking the Northern Wei, addressed the emperor as "Your Foot," and referred to himself as "I."

sentences.zh: 獻師子皮袴褶，皮如虎皮，色白毛短。

translations.literal: He presented a lion-skin jacket and trousers; the hide was like tiger skin, white in color with short hair.
translations.idiomatic: He presented a jacket-and-trousers set of supposed lion skin; the hide resembled tiger skin, pale in color with short fur.

sentences.zh: 時有賈胡在蜀見之，云此非師子皮，乃扶拔皮也。

translations.literal: At the time a merchant from abroad in Shu saw it and said this was not lion skin but baboon skin.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign merchant then in Shu saw it and said it was not lion skin at all but baboon hide.

sentences.zh: 國相邢基祇羅迴奉表曰：

translations.literal: The state chancellor Xingjizhiluo Hui presented a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran chancellor Xingjizhiluo Hui submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 夫四象稟政，二儀改度，而萬物生焉。

translations.literal: The four images receive governance; the two principles change their measure, and the ten thousand things are thereby born.
translations.idiomatic: The four emblems take up the mandate of rule, the two cosmic principles shift their measure, and the ten thousand things come into being.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋虧盈迭襲，歷數自然也。

translations.literal: This is surely the succession of waning and waxing in turn—the natural course of dynastic numbers.
translations.idiomatic: This is nothing but the alternation of decline and fullness, the natural rhythm of dynastic fortune.

sentences.zh: 昔晉室將終，楚桓竊命，寔賴宋武匡濟之功，故能扶衰定傾，休否以泰。

translations.literal: Formerly when the Jin house was about to end, Chu Huan usurped the mandate; it truly relied on Song Wu's merit in righting the age, and therefore was able to support the declining and settle the tipping, turning adversity into peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin house neared its end, Huan Wen of Chu seized power; it was Song Wu Di's work of rescue that propped up a failing dynasty, steadied a tottering state, and turned misfortune into prosperity.

sentences.zh: 祚流九葉，而國嗣不繼。

translations.literal: The throne passed through nine generations, yet the succession of the state did not continue.
translations.idiomatic: The throne passed through nine generations, yet the line of succession broke off.

sentences.zh: 今皇天降禍於上，宋室猜亂于下。

translations.literal: Now Heaven above sends calamity, and the Song house below is suspicious and in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven has sent down calamity from above, while the Song house below is riven by suspicion and turmoil.

sentences.zh: 臣雖荒遠，粗闚圖書，數難以來，星文改度，房心受變，虛危納祉，宋滅齊昌，此其驗也。

translations.literal: Your servant, though remote and barbarous, has roughly glimpsed the charts and books; since calamities have come in succession, the star writings have changed their degrees—Fang and Xin received transformation, Xu and Wei received blessing—Song perished and Qi flourished: this is the proof.
translations.idiomatic: Though I dwell in a distant land, I have gleaned something from the charts and classics: as disasters have piled up one after another, the stars have shifted their stations—Fang and Xin have changed, Xu and Wei have taken in good fortune—Song is destroyed and Qi rises: this is the proof.

sentences.zh: 水運遘屯，木德應運，子年垂刈，劉穆之記，崏嶺有不衽之山，京房讖云「卯金十六，草肅應王」。

translations.literal: The Water Phase's fortune meets obstruction; the Wood Virtue responds to the mandate; the zi year approaches harvest; Liu Muzhi's record; on Mount Min there is a mountain of unlapped robes; Jing Fang's prophecy says, "Mao-metal sixteen, grass-su responds as king."
translations.idiomatic: The fortune of Water meets obstruction; the virtue of Wood answers the times; the zi year is ripe for the reaping; so runs Liu Muzhi's record; on Mount Min stands the Mountain of Unlapped Robes; and Jing Fang's prophecy reads, "Mao-metal at sixteen—grass and su shall answer as king."

sentences.zh: 歷觀圖緯，休徵非一，皆云慶鍾蕭氏，代宋者齊。

translations.literal: Reviewing the charts and weft-texts throughout, auspicious signs are not one alone; all say blessing concentrates on the Xiao clan—he who replaces Song is Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the prognostic charts and weft-texts, the auspicious omens are many, and all declare that fortune will settle on the house of Xiao—that Qi is destined to replace Song.

sentences.zh: 會有使力法度及△此國使反，採訪聖德，彌驗天縱之姿。

translations.literal: It happened that the envoy Li Fadu and [lacuna] envoys of this state returned, inquiring into sagely virtue and confirming all the more a heaven-endowed bearing.
translations.idiomatic: By chance the envoy Li Fadu and other envoys of your state returned from their missions; in seeking out your sagely virtue they confirmed all the more your heaven-endowed excellence.

sentences.zh: 故能挾隆皇祚，光權定之業，翼亮天功，濟悖主之難。

translations.literal: Therefore you were able to embrace the exalted imperial succession, glorify the enterprise of settling authority, assist and brighten Heaven's achievement, and rescue the difficulty of a perverse lord.
translations.idiomatic: Thus you could uphold the exalted imperial succession, bring glory to the work of securing the realm, aid Heaven's achievement, and deliver the realm from a wayward ruler's peril.

sentences.zh: 樹勳京師，威振海外。

translations.literal: You planted merit in the capital; your awe shook lands beyond the seas.
translations.idiomatic: You built up merit in the capital, and your prestige shook the lands beyond the seas.

sentences.zh: 杖義之功，侔縱湯、武。

translations.literal: The achievement of upholding righteousness was equal to Tang and Wu of old.
translations.idiomatic: Your righteous achievement matched that of Tang and Wu.

sentences.zh: 冥績旣著，寶命因歸，受終之曆，歸于有道。

translations.literal: Hidden merit having been displayed, the precious mandate thereby returned; the calendar of receiving the end belonged to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Once your hidden merit had shone forth, the precious mandate returned to you; the calendar of succession passed to the one who holds the Way.

sentences.zh: 況夫帝無常族，有德必昌，時來之數，唯靈是與。

translations.literal: Moreover, emperorship has no fixed clan; those with virtue must flourish—the number of the time come shares only with the numinous.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the throne has no fixed house: those with virtue must prosper, and the fortune of the age belongs only to the worthy spirit.

sentences.zh: 陛下承乾啓之機，因乘龍之運，計應符革祚，久已踐極，荒裔傾戴，莫不引領。

translations.literal: Your Majesty inherited the opportunity of Qian's opening and rode the fortune of the dragon's ascent; by reckoning you matched the omen to change the throne and long since trod the ultimate—barbarian lands lean in allegiance, none not stretching their necks.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty seized the opening granted by Heaven and rode the dragon's fortune; by every reckoning you matched the omens to change the dynasty and have long since ascended the throne, while distant lands bow in allegiance and all stretch their necks in hope.

sentences.zh: 設未龍飛，不宜沖挹，上違天人之心，下乖黎庶之望。

translations.literal: If you have not yet flown as the dragon, it is not fitting to hold back in humility—above you would violate the hearts of Heaven and man, below you would go against the hopes of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: If the dragon has not yet taken flight, it is wrong to hold yourself back: above, you would defy the hearts of Heaven and men; below, you would betray the people's hopes.

sentences.zh: 皇芮承緒，肇自二儀，拓土載民，地越滄海，百代一族，大業天固。

translations.literal: Imperial Rouran received the succession, beginning from the two principles; it expanded territory and bore the people, its land crossing the blue sea—a single clan for a hundred generations, great enterprise heaven-firmed.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Rouran inherits its line from the two cosmic principles, has broadened its lands and borne its people across the blue sea, remains one clan through a hundred generations, and its great enterprise is secured by Heaven.

sentences.zh: 雖吳漠殊域，義同脣齒，方欲剋期中原，龔行天罰。

translations.literal: Although Wu and the desert are different regions, in righteousness we are like lips and teeth; we are just about to set a date for the Central Plains and reverently carry out Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Though our lands lie far apart, we are as close as lips and teeth in purpose, and we mean to fix a day to march on the Central Plains and reverently execute Heaven's punishment.

sentences.zh: 治兵繕甲，俟時大舉。

translations.literal: We drill troops and repair armor, awaiting the time for a great campaign.
translations.idiomatic: We are drilling troops and repairing armor, waiting for the moment to strike in force.

sentences.zh: 振霜戈於幷、代，鳴和鈴於秦、趙，掃殄凶醜，梟剪元惡。

translations.literal: We will shake frost-bright spears in Bing and Dai, ring harmony bells in Qin and Zhao, sweep away the vicious and ugly, and behead and cut down the chief villain.
translations.idiomatic: We shall brandish our spears in Bing and Dai, sound our war bells in Qin and Zhao, sweep away the wicked, and cut down the arch-enemy.

sentences.zh: 然後皇輿遷幸，光復中華，永敦隣好，侔蹤齊、魯。

translations.literal: Then the imperial carriage will move in residence, restoring brilliance to China, forever thickening neighborly good will, matching the tracks of Qi and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Then the imperial carriage may move north, the Central Plains will be restored, and we shall keep neighborly peace forever, matching the friendship of Qi and Lu.

sentences.zh: 使四海有奉，蒼生咸賴，荒餘歸仰，豈不盛哉！

translations.literal: Let the four seas have whom to serve, the dark-haired people all rely, and the wastes and remnants return in reverence—is this not magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Let the four seas have a ruler to serve, let all people find refuge, and let the far wastes look up in allegiance—what glory could be greater!

sentences.zh: 芮芮王求醫工等物，世祖詔報曰：「知須醫及織成錦工、指南車、漏刻，竝非所愛。

translations.literal: The Rouran king requested physicians and other things; Emperor Shizu replied by edict: "We know you need physicians and brocade-weaving craftsmen, the south-pointing carriage, and the clepsydra—all are not what we favor sending."
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran king asked for physicians and other items. Emperor Wu replied by edict: "We know you need physicians, brocade weavers, a south-pointing carriage, and a clepsydra—none of these are things we are willing to provide."

sentences.zh: 南方治疾，與北土不同。

translations.literal: In the south, treating illness differs from the northern soil.
translations.idiomatic: Medicine in the south differs from practice in the north.

sentences.zh: 織成錦工，竝女人，不堪涉遠。

translations.literal: Brocade-weaving craftsmen are all women and cannot bear to travel far.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade weavers are all women and cannot endure a long journey.

sentences.zh: 指南車、漏刻，此雖有其器，工匠久不復存，不副爲誤。」

translations.literal: As for the south-pointing carriage and clepsydra, although these devices exist, the craftsmen have long ceased to exist—it would not suit to send them in error."
translations.idiomatic: As for the south-pointing carriage and clepsydra, although the devices exist, the craftsmen who made them have long since vanished; it would be a mistake to send them."

sentences.zh: 自芮芮居匈奴故庭，十年，丁零胡又南攻芮芮，得其故地，芮芮稍南徙。

translations.literal: From the time the Rouran dwelt in the former Xiongnu court, after ten years the Dingling Hu again attacked the Rouran from the south, obtained their former territory, and the Rouran gradually moved south.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years after the Rouran settled in the old Xiongnu heartland, the Dingling Hu attacked them from the south, seized that territory, and the Rouran gradually shifted southward.

sentences.zh: 魏虜主元宏以其侵逼，遣偽平元王駕鹿渾、龍驤將軍楊延數十萬騎伐芮芮，大寒雪，人馬死者衆。

translations.literal: The Wei barbarian lord Yuan Hong, because of their encroachment and pressure, sent the false Prince of Pingyuan Jialuhun and General of the Dragon Charger Yang Yan with several hundred thousand horsemen to attack the Rouran; great cold and snow fell, and many men and horses died.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler Yuan Hong, angered by their encroachments, sent the puppet Prince of Pingyuan Jialuhun and Dragon Charger General Yang Yan with several hundred thousand horsemen against the Rouran; bitter cold and snow killed multitudes of men and horses.

sentences.zh: 先是益州刺史劉悛遣使江景玄使丁零，宣國威德。

translations.literal: Earlier the Inspector of Yizhou Liu Jun sent the envoy Jiang Jingxuan to mission to the Dingling, proclaiming the state's majesty and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Jun, inspector of Yizhou, sent the envoy Jiang Jingxuan to the Dingling to proclaim the empire's majesty and virtue.

sentences.zh: 道經鄯善、于闐，鄯善爲丁零所破，人民散盡。

translations.literal: On the road he passed Shanshan and Yutian; Shanshan had been broken by the Dingling and its people scattered to the end.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through Shanshan and Khotan; Shanshan had been overrun by the Dingling and its people scattered.

sentences.zh: 于闐尤信佛法。

translations.literal: Yutian especially believed in the Buddhist Law.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan was especially devoted to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 丁零僭稱天子，勞接景玄使，反命。

translations.literal: The Dingling presumptuously styled themselves Son of Heaven, received and entertained Envoy Jingxuan with courtesy, and he returned with his report.
translations.idiomatic: The Dingling had presumptuously styled themselves Son of Heaven; they received Envoy Jingxuan with courtesy, and he returned to report.

sentences.zh: 芮芮常由河南道而抵益州。

translations.literal: The Rouran commonly came by the Henan route to reach Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran commonly traveled the Henan route to reach Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 河南，匈奴種也。

translations.literal: Henan were a Xiongnu race.
translations.idiomatic: Henan was a Xiongnu people.

sentences.zh: 漢建武中，匈奴奴婢亡匿在涼州界雜種數千人，虜名奴婢爲貲，一謂之「貲虜」。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era of Han, several thousand Xiongnu slave men and women fled and hid among miscellaneous peoples on the border of Liangzhou; the barbarians called slave men and women "property," and they were also called "Property Barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu reign of Han, several thousand Xiongnu slaves fled and hid among mixed peoples on the Liangzhou frontier; the barbarians called slaves "property," whence the name "Property Barbarians."

sentences.zh: 鮮卑慕容廆庶兄吐谷渾爲氐王。

translations.literal: Murong Hui of the Xianbei's younger brother by a concubine, Tuyuhun, became king of the Di.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun, a younger half-brother of the Xianbei Murong Hui, became king of the Di.

sentences.zh: 在益州西北，亘數千里。

translations.literal: They were northwest of Yizhou, stretching several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: They lay northwest of Yizhou and stretched for thousands of li.

sentences.zh: 其南界龍涸城，去成都千餘里。

translations.literal: Their southern border was Longgu City, more than a thousand li from Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Their southern border was Longgu City, over a thousand li from Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 大戍有四，一在清水川，一在赤水，一在澆河，一在吐屈真川，皆子弟所治。

translations.literal: There were four great garrisons—one at Qingshui River, one at Chishui, one at Jiao River, one at Tuquzhen River—all administered by sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: They maintained four major garrisons—at Qingshui River, Chishui, Jiao River, and Tuquzhen River—each governed by a royal son or younger brother.

sentences.zh: 其王治慕駕川。

translations.literal: Their king ruled from Mujia River.
translations.idiomatic: The king ruled from Mujia River.

sentences.zh: 多畜，逐水草，無城郭。

translations.literal: They kept much livestock, followed water and pasture, and had no walls or towns.
translations.idiomatic: They raised many herds, followed pasture and water, and had no walled towns.

sentences.zh: 後稍爲宮屋，而人民猶以氈廬百子帳爲行屋。

translations.literal: Later they gradually built palace houses, yet the people still used felt huts and hundred-son tents as traveling dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: They later built palaces of a sort, but the people still used felt tents and "hundred-son" marquees as their traveling homes.

sentences.zh: 地常風寒，人行平沙中，沙礫飛起，行迹皆滅。

translations.literal: The land was constantly windy and cold; when people walked on level sand, gravel flew up and all tracks were erased.
translations.idiomatic: The land was perpetually windy and cold; when travelers crossed level sands, flying grit erased every footprint.

sentences.zh: 肥地則有雀鼠同穴，生黃紫花；

translations.literal: On fertile ground sparrows and rats shared one burrow and yellow and purple flowers grew;
translations.idiomatic: On fertile ground sparrows and rats shared one burrow and yellow and purple flowers grew;

sentences.zh: 瘦地輙有鄣氣，使人斷氣，牛馬得之，疲汗不能行。

translations.literal: on lean ground there were often barrier miasmas that made men lose their breath; cattle and horses that got them grew weary and sweated and could not walk.
translations.idiomatic: on barren ground there was often a choking miasma that stopped men's breath; cattle and horses that breathed it grew weak, sweated, and could not go on.

sentences.zh: 宋初始受爵命，至宋末，河南王吐谷渾拾寅爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督西秦河沙三州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、領護羌校尉、西秦河二州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song they first received titles and commands; by the end of Song, the King of Henan Tuyuhun Shiyin was Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander of all military affairs of the three provinces Xi-Qin-He-Sha, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master with golden seal and purple ribbon opening an office equal to the Three Excellencies, Colonel Protector of the Qiang, and Inspector of the two provinces Xi-Qin-He.
translations.idiomatic: They first received titles and commissions under the Song; by the end of Song, King of Henan Tuyuhun Shiyin held the posts of Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander of Military Affairs in the Three Provinces of Western Qin, He, and Sha, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master with golden seal opening an office equal to the Three Excellencies, Colonel Protector of the Qiang, and Inspector of Western Qin and He.

sentences.zh: 拾寅子易度侯好星文，嘗求星書，朝議不給。

translations.literal: Shiyin's son Yiduhou loved astral writings and once requested star books; court deliberation did not grant them.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyin's son Yiduhou was fond of astronomy and once asked for star charts; the court refused to supply them.

sentences.zh: 寅卒，三年，以河南王世子吐谷渾易度侯爲使持節、都督西秦河沙三州諸軍事、鎮西將軍、領護羌校尉、西秦河二州刺史、河南王。

translations.literal: When Yin died, in the third year they made the Heir of the King of Henan Tuyuhun Yiduhou Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of the three provinces Xi-Qin-He-Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protector of the Qiang, Inspector of the two provinces Xi-Qin-He, and King of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiyin died, in the third year the heir of the King of Henan, Tuyuhun Yiduhou, was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs in the Three Provinces of Western Qin, He, and Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protector of the Qiang, Inspector of Western Qin and He, and King of Henan.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，詔曰：「易度侯守職西蕃，綏懷允緝，忠績兼舉，朕有嘉焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming, an edict said: "Yiduhou guards his post in the western borderlands, pacifies and cherishes with true harmony, and loyalty and achievement are both displayed—we are pleased."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming, an edict read: "Yiduhou has kept his post on the western frontier, ruled with true harmony, and shown both loyalty and merit—we commend him."

sentences.zh: 可進號車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: He may advance in title to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He is promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 」遣給事中丘冠先使河南道，幷送芮芮使。

translations.literal: " They sent the Attendant Within the Yellow Gate Qiu Guanxian as envoy on the Henan route, and also to escort the Rouran envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Attendant Within Qiu Guanxian on the Henan route and also to escort the Rouran envoy.

sentences.zh: 至六年乃還。

translations.literal: He returned only in the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: He did not return until the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 得玉長三尺二寸，厚一尺一寸。

translations.literal: He obtained jade three chi two cun long and one chi one cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: He brought back a jade slab three chi two cun long and one chi one cun thick.

sentences.zh: 易度侯卒，八年，立其世子休留茂爲使持節、督西秦河沙三州諸軍事、鎮西將軍、領護羌校尉、西秦河二州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yiduhou died, in the eighth year they established his heir Xiulumao as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of all military affairs of the three provinces Xi-Qin-He-Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protector of the Qiang, and Inspector of the two provinces Xi-Qin-He.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiduhou died, in the eighth year his heir Xiulumao was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in the Three Provinces of Western Qin, He, and Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protector of the Qiang, and Inspector of Western Qin and He.

sentences.zh: 復遣振武將軍丘冠先拜授，幷行弔禮。

translations.literal: They again sent General Who Quells Martial Qiu Guanxian to confer the appointment and also perform mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: The court again sent General Who Quells Martial Qiu Guanxian to invest him and offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 冠先至河南，休留茂逼令先拜，冠先厲色不肯，休留茂恥其國人，執冠先於絕巖上推墮深谷而死。

translations.literal: When Guanxian reached Henan, Xiulumao forced him to bow first; Guanxian sternly refused. Xiulumao, shamed before his countrymen, seized Guanxian on a sheer cliff, pushed him off, and he fell into a deep ravine and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanxian reached Henan, Xiulumao tried to force him to bow first; Guanxian sternly refused. Ashamed before his people, Xiulumao seized him on a sheer cliff, pushed him into a deep ravine, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 冠先字道玄，吳興人，晉吏部郎傑六世孫也。

translations.literal: Guanxian's style was Daoxuan; he was a man of Wuxing, sixth-generation descendant of the Jin Minister of the Civil Service Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Guanxian, styled Daoxuan, was from Wuxing and a sixth-generation descendant of Jie, Minister of the Civil Service under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 上初遣冠先，示尚書令王儉，儉答上曰：「此人不啻堪行。

translations.literal: When the emperor first sent Guanxian, he showed him to the Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian; Jian answered the emperor: "This man is not merely fit for the mission."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first chose Guanxian, he showed him to Director Wang Jian, who told the throne: "This man is more than fit for the mission."

sentences.zh: 」乃再銜命。

translations.literal: " Therefore he received the command a second time.
translations.idiomatic: So he was sent out again.

sentences.zh: 及死，世祖敕其子雄曰：「卿父受使河南，秉忠守死，不辱王命，我甚賞惜，喪屍絕域，不可復尋，於卿後宦塗無妨，甚有高比。

translations.literal: When he died, Emperor Shizu instructed his son Xiong: "Your father received the mission to Henan, held loyalty and kept death, and did not disgrace the royal command—we greatly prize and mourn him. His corpse lies in a distant land and cannot be sought again; your later official career will not be hindered—you have a very high comparison."
translations.idiomatic: After his death, Emperor Wu instructed his son Xiong: "Your father took the mission to Henan, kept faith unto death, and did not dishonor the imperial command. I prize and mourn him deeply. His body lies in a far land and cannot be recovered, but your official career will not suffer—you have a father to be proud of."

sentences.zh: 」賜錢十萬，布三十匹。

translations.literal: " He granted one hundred thousand cash and thirty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one hundred thousand cash and thirty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 氐楊氏，與苻氐同出略陽，漢世居仇池，地號百頃。

translations.literal: The Di clan Yang, together with the Fu Di, came forth from Lueyang; in the Han era they dwelt at Chouchi, a place called Hundred-Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang clan of the Di, kin to the Fu Di, came from Lueyang; in Han times they lived at Chouchi, a place called Hundred Qing.

sentences.zh: 建安中，有百頃氐王是也。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an era there was the King of the Hundred-Qing Di—this was he.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jian'an era there was a King of the Hundred-Qing Di—this was that line.

sentences.zh: 晉世有楊茂，後轉彊盛，事見前史。

translations.literal: In the Jin era there was Yang Mao; later they turned powerful and flourishing—the affairs are seen in earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin era there was Yang Mao; the clan later grew powerful—events are recorded in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 仇池四方壁立，自然有樓櫓却敵狀，高竝數丈。

translations.literal: Chouchi on all four sides stood like walls; naturally it had the form of towered ramparts to repel enemies, heights together several zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Chouchi rose on all sides like sheer walls, naturally forming towered ramparts to repel attack, several zhang high.

sentences.zh: 有二十二道可攀緣而升，東西二門，盤道可七里。

translations.literal: There were twenty-two paths by which one could climb and ascend; east and west two gates; the winding path was about seven li.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two paths allowed climbers to ascend; there were east and west gates, and the winding road ran about seven li.

sentences.zh: 上有岡阜泉源。

translations.literal: Above were hillocks, mounds, and spring sources.
translations.idiomatic: Above were hills and springs.

sentences.zh: 氐於上平地立宮室果園倉庫，無貴賤皆爲板屋土牆，所治處名洛谷。

translations.literal: The Di on the upper level ground built palaces, orchards, and storehouses; without distinction of noble and base all had plank houses and earthen walls; the place they governed was called Luogu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: On the plateau the Di built palaces, orchards, and storehouses; nobles and commoners alike lived in plank houses with earthen walls; their seat was called Luogu Valley.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉十九年，龍驤將軍裴方明等伐氐，剋仇池，後爲魏虜所攻，失地。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia of Song, General of the Dragon Charger Pei Fangming and others attacked the Di, took Chouchi, but later were attacked by the Wei barbarians and lost the territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia of Song, Dragon Charger General Pei Fangming and others attacked the Di and took Chouchi, but later the Northern Wei attacked them and they lost the territory.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊難當從兄子文德聚衆茄蘆，宋世加以爵位。

translations.literal: The Di king Yang Nan-dang's cousin's son Wende gathered a host at Jialu; in the Song era titles and ranks were added to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wende, a cousin's son of the Di king Yang Nandang, gathered forces at Jialu and received titles under the Song.

sentences.zh: 文德死，從弟僧嗣、文慶傳代之。

translations.literal: When Wende died, his younger cousins Sengsi and Wenqing succeeded him in turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Wende died, his younger cousins Sengsi and Wenqing succeeded him in turn.

sentences.zh: 難當族弟廣香先奔虜，元徽中，爲虜攻殺文慶，以爲陰平公、茄蘆鎮主。

translations.literal: Nandang's clansman younger brother Guangxiang first fled to the barbarians; in the Yuanhui era he attacked and killed Wenqing for the barbarians and was made Duke of Yinping and chief of Jialu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang's clansman Guangxiang had earlier fled to the Northern Wei; in the Yuanhui era he attacked and killed Wenqing for them and was made Duke of Yinping and commander of Jialu.

sentences.zh: 文慶從弟文弘爲白水太守，屯武興，朝議以爲輔國將軍、北秦州刺史、武都王仇池公。

translations.literal: Wenqing's younger cousin Wenhong was Administrator of Baishui, encamped at Wuxing; court deliberation made him General Who Assists the State, Inspector of Northern Qinzhou, King of Wudou, and Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing's younger cousin Wenhong was administrator of Baishui and encamped at Wuxing; the court appointed him General Who Assists the State, Inspector of Northern Qin, King of Wudu, and Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史范柏年被誅，其親將李烏奴懼奔叛，文弘納之。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Liangzhou Fan Bonian was executed; his close general Li Wunu feared and fled in rebellion; Wenhong received him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bonian, inspector of Liangzhou, was executed; his trusted officer Li Wunu, fearing for his life, fled in rebellion, and Wenhong took him in.

sentences.zh: 烏奴率亡命千餘人攻梁州，爲刺史王玄邈所破，復走還氐中。

translations.literal: Wunu led more than a thousand desperate men to attack Liangzhou, was broken by the Inspector Wang Xuanyao, and again fled back among the Di.
translations.idiomatic: Wunu led more than a thousand desperate men against Liangzhou, was defeated by Inspector Wang Xuanyao, and fled back to the Di lands.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史豫章王嶷遣兵討烏奴，檄梁州能斬送烏奴首，賞本郡，烏奴田宅事業悉賜之。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jingzhou the Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Yi sent troops to punish Wunu, proclaiming that Liangzhou, if able to behead and deliver Wunu's head, would be rewarded with its native commandery and all of Wunu's fields, houses, and enterprises would be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi, Prince of Yuzhang and inspector of Jingzhou, sent troops against Wunu and proclaimed that whoever in Liangzhou could deliver Wunu's head would receive his native commandery and all his lands and property.

sentences.zh: 與廣香書曰：

translations.literal: He wrote to Guangxiang, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Guangxiang:

sentences.zh: 夫廢興無謬，逆順有恒，古今共貫；

translations.literal: Rise and fall are without error; compliance and rebellion have a constant—the ancient and modern share one thread;
translations.idiomatic: Rise and fall follow no mistake; loyalty and rebellion have their constant law—past and present share one thread;

sentences.zh: 賢愚同察。

translations.literal: the worthy and foolish observe alike.
translations.idiomatic: the wise and the foolish see alike.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史范柏年懷挾詭態，首鼠兩端，旣已被伐，盤桓稽命。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Liangzhou Fan Bonian harbored deceitful attitudes, was a rat with head to both ends; having already been punished, he lingered and delayed his fate.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bonian, inspector of Liangzhou, harbored treacherous designs and wavered between two sides; though already punished, he lingered and delayed his end.

sentences.zh: 遂潛遣李烏奴叛。

translations.literal: He then secretly sent Li Wunu to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly sent Li Wunu into rebellion.

sentences.zh: 楊文弘扇誘邊疆荒雜。

translations.literal: Yang Wenhong fanned and enticed the borderland wastes and mixed peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wenhong stirred up the mixed peoples of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 柏年今已梟禽，烏奴頻被摧破，計其餘燼，行自消夷。

translations.literal: Bonian has now been beheaded and captured; Wunu has repeatedly been shattered and broken—reckoning their remaining embers, they will soon extinguish of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Bonian has already been executed; Wunu has been repeatedly defeated—their remaining embers will soon die out on their own.

sentences.zh: 今遣參軍行晉壽太守王道寶、參軍事行北巴西新巴二郡太守任湜之、行宕渠太守王安會領銳卒三千，遄塗風邁，浮川電掩。

translations.literal: Now we send the Aide-de-Camp acting Administrator of Jinshou Wang Daobao, the Staff Officer acting Administrator of the two commanderies Northern Ba-Xi and Xin-Ba Ren Mizhi, and the acting Administrator of Dangqu Wang Anhui leading three thousand sharp troops—swift on the road like the wind, crossing rivers like lightning's cover.
translations.idiomatic: We now send Aide Wang Daobao, acting administrator of Jinshou; Staff Officer Ren Mizhi, acting administrator of Northern Ba-Xi and Xin-Ba; and acting administrator of Dangqu Wang Anhui, leading three thousand elite troops—swift as the wind on the road, lightning over the rivers.

sentences.zh: 又命輔國將軍三巴校尉明惠照、巴郡太守魯休烈、南巴西太守柳弘稱、益州刺史傅琰，竝簡徒競騖，選甲爭馳。

translations.literal: We also order General Who Assists the State and Colonel of Sanba Ming Huizhao, Administrator of Ba Commandery Lu Xiulie, Administrator of Southern Ba-Xi Liu Hongcheng, and Inspector of Yizhou Fu Yan—all to select troops in competing haste, choose armor in striving gallop.
translations.idiomatic: We also order General Who Assists the State and Colonel of Sanba Ming Huizhao, Administrator of Ba Lu Xiulie, Administrator of Southern Ba-Xi Liu Hongcheng, and Inspector of Yizhou Fu Yan—all to muster their forces at full speed and rush their best troops forward.

sentences.zh: 雍州水步，行次魏興，幷山東僑舊，會于南鄭。

translations.literal: Yongzhou's water and foot [forces], marching in sequence to Weixing, together with eastern mountain émigré veterans, will meet at Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou's river and land forces will march by stages to Weixing, and together with the eastern émigré levies will assemble at Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 或汎舟墊江，或飛旍劔道，腹背飆騰，表裏震擊。

translations.literal: Some sailed boats on the Dian River, others flew banners along the Sword Road; front and rear surged like gales, inner and outer struck in shock.
translations.idiomatic: Some forces sailed the Dian River, others raced banners along the Sword Road—striking from front and rear like a gale, hammering within and without.

sentences.zh: 文弘容納叛戾，專爲淵藪，外侮皇威，內凌國族。

translations.literal: Wenhong harbored rebels and outlaws, making himself a deep lair; outwardly he insulted imperial majesty, inwardly he bullied the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhong sheltered rebels and outlaws, turning his domain into a rebel nest; he affronted imperial authority abroad and bullied the imperial clan at home.

sentences.zh: 君弈世忠款，深識理順，想卽起義，應接大軍，共爲掎角，討滅烏奴，剋建忠勤，茂立誠節。

translations.literal: My lord, your house for generations has been loyal and sincere, deeply knowing what reason and compliance require; we expect you at once to rise in righteous action, meet our great army, together form pincers, destroy Wunu, achieve merit in loyalty and diligence, and abundantly establish sincere integrity.
translations.idiomatic: You have been loyal for generations and understand where duty lies; we expect you to rise at once, join our main army in a pincer movement, destroy Wunu, win merit through loyalty, and stand as a model of integrity.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之資十年之積，權百旅之衆，師出境而城潰，兵未戰而自屠，朝廷無遺鏃之費，士民靡傷痍之弊。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi relied on ten years' accumulation and commanded the hosts of a hundred brigades—his army left the borders and cities collapsed, troops had not fought and they slaughtered themselves; the court spent not a leftover arrow's cost, officers and people suffered no wound of harm.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi had ten years of buildup and commanded armies a hundred brigades strong—yet his forces barely crossed the border before cities fell, and his men destroyed themselves without a battle; the court spent scarcely an arrow, and the people suffered hardly a wound.

sentences.zh: 況蕞爾小豎，方之篾如，其取殲殄，豈延漏刻。

translations.literal: How much more this tiny villain, compared to whom he is like a splinter—his capture and extinction could not delay even a quarter-hour.
translations.idiomatic: As for this petty rebel, he is not even a splinter beside Shen Youzhi—his destruction cannot take more than a moment.

sentences.zh: 忝以寡昧，分陝司蕃，清氛蕩穢，諒惟任職。

translations.literal: I am unworthy in my slight dullness, dividing Shaan and overseeing the frontier; to clear the air and sweep away filth is surely my charge.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am unworthy in my limited wisdom, I oversee the frontier and must clear away this corruption—that is my duty.

sentences.zh: 此府器械山積，戈旗林聳，士卒剽勁，蓄銳權威，除難剿寇，豈俟徵習！

translations.literal: This prefecture's weapons pile like mountains, spears and banners stand like forests, soldiers are fierce and sharp, stored edge and stored authority—destroying difficulty and cutting down bandits, how wait for mobilization and drill!
translations.idiomatic: This commandery's arms are heaped like mountains, its banners stand like a forest, its troops are fierce and ready—when cutting down rebels, why wait for drill!

sentences.zh: 但以剪伐萌菌，弗勞洪斧，撲彼蚊蚋，無假多力。

translations.literal: It is only that cutting down sprouting fungus does not weary the great axe; swatting those mosquitoes needs no extra force.
translations.idiomatic: This is only clearing away sprouts—no need for the great axe; swatting gnats requires no great effort.

sentences.zh: 皇上聖哲應期，恩澤廣被，罪止首惡，餘無所問。

translations.literal: The emperor is sagely and wise, responding to the age; grace spreads widely; guilt stops at the chief villain, the rest are not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Our sage emperor answers the times, and his grace is wide; guilt rests on the ringleader alone, and the rest will not be punished.

sentences.zh: 賞罰之科，具寫如別。

translations.literal: The categories of reward and punishment are fully written as attached.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments are set forth in the attached schedule.

sentences.zh: 使道寶步出魏興，分軍泝墊江，俱會晉壽。

translations.literal: The envoy Daobao marched out from Weixing, divided the army to ascend the Dian River, and all met at Jinshou.
translations.idiomatic: Daobao marched out from Weixing, sent detachments up the Dian River, and all converged on Jinshou.

sentences.zh: 太祖以文弘背叛，進廣香爲持節、都督西秦州刺史。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, because Wenhong rebelled, advanced Guangxiang to Bearer of the Staff and Commander of Western Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wenhong had rebelled, the Founding Emperor promoted Guangxiang to Bearer of the Staff and Commander of Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 廣香子北部鎮將軍郡事炅爲征虜將軍、武都太守。

translations.literal: Guangxiang's son, the northern garrison general in charge of commandery affairs Jiong, was made General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Administrator of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxiang's son Jiong, who handled commandery affairs at the northern garrison, was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and administrator of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 以難當正胤楊後起爲持節、寧朔將軍、平羌校尉、北秦州刺史、武都王，鎮武興，卽文弘從兄子也。

translations.literal: They made Nandang's legitimate heir Yang Houqi Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Northern Qinzhou, and King of Wudu, stationed at Wuxing—he was Wenhong's cousin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang's legitimate heir Yang Houqi was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Northern Qin, and King of Wudu, with his seat at Wuxing—Wenhong's cousin's son.

sentences.zh: 三年，文弘歸降，復以爲征西將軍、北秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year, Wenhong returned in submission and was again made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Northern Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Wenhong submitted again and was reappointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Northern Qin.

sentences.zh: 先是廣香病死，氐衆半奔文弘，半詣梁州刺史崔慧景。

translations.literal: Earlier Guangxiang had died of illness; half the Di host fled to Wenhong, half went to the Inspector of Liangzhou Cui Huijing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guangxiang had died; half the Di people went to Wenhong and half to Cui Huijing, inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 文弘遣從子後起進據白水。

translations.literal: Wenhong sent his cousin's son Houqi forward to seize Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhong sent his cousin's son Houqi to advance and occupy Baishui.

sentences.zh: 白水居晉壽上流，西接涪界，東帶益路，北連陰平、茄蘆，爲形勝之地。

translations.literal: Baishui lay upstream of Jinshou, west connecting to Fu territory, east bordering the road to Yi, north linking Yinping and Jialu—a place of strategic advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Baishui lay upstream from Jinshou, bordered Fu to the west and the Yi road to the east, and linked Yinping and Jialu to the north—a strategic strongpoint.

sentences.zh: 晉壽太守楊公則啓經略之宜，上答曰：「文弘罪不可恕，事中政應且加恩耳。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Jinshou Yang Gongze memorialized on the proper strategy; the emperor answered: "Wenhong's crime cannot be forgiven, yet in the affair the government should for the moment add grace."
translations.idiomatic: Jinshou administrator Yang Gongze submitted a plan of campaign; the emperor replied: "Wenhong's crime cannot be forgiven, yet for now the court should show him some grace."

sentences.zh: 卿若能襲破白水，必加厚賞。」

translations.literal: "If you can surprise and take Baishui, rewards will surely be greatly increased."
translations.idiomatic: "If you can storm and take Baishui, your reward will be greatly increased."

sentences.zh: 十年，集始反，率氐、蜀雜衆寇漢川，梁州刺史陰智伯遣軍主寧朔將軍桓盧奴、梁季羣、宋△、王士隆等千餘人拒之，不利，退保白馬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Jishi rebelled, leading Di and Shu mixed hosts to raid Hanchuan; the Inspector of Liangzhou Yin Zhibo sent the commanders Colonel Who Pacifies the North Huan Lunu, Liang Jiqun, Song [lacuna], Wang Shilong, and others with more than a thousand men to resist—without success, they withdrew to defend Baima.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Jishi rebelled and led Di and Shu mixed forces against Hanchuan; Yin Zhibo, inspector of Liangzhou, sent commanders including Colonel Who Pacifies the North Huan Lunu, Liang Jiqun, Song [name missing], and Wang Shilong with over a thousand men to resist; they failed and fell back to defend Baima.

sentences.zh: 賊衆萬餘人縱兵火攻其城柵，盧奴拒守死戰。

translations.literal: The rebel host of more than ten thousand men loosed troops and fire to attack their palisade; Lunu resisted and defended, fighting to the death.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand rebels attacked the palisade with fire; Lunu held the defense and fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 智伯又遣軍主陰仲昌等馬步數千人救援。

translations.literal: Zhibo again sent the commanders Yin Zhongchang and others with several thousand horse and foot to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibo sent Yin Zhongchang and other commanders with several thousand cavalry and infantry to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 至白馬城東千溪橋，相去數里，集始等悉力攻之，官軍內外奮擊，集始大敗，十八營一時潰走，殺獲數千人。

translations.literal: When they reached the Qianxi Bridge east of Baima City, several li apart, Jishi and the others attacked with all their strength; the government troops struck fiercely within and without; Jishi was greatly defeated, eighteen camps fled at once, and several thousand were killed or captured.
translations.idiomatic: At the Qianxi Bridge east of Baima, a few li away, Jishi attacked with full force; government troops struck from within and without; Jishi was routed, eighteen camps fled at once, and several thousand were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 集始奔入虜堺。

translations.literal: Jishi fled into the barbarian frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi fled into Northern Wei territory.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，以前將軍楊炅爲使持節、督沙州諸軍事、平西將軍、平羌校尉、沙州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang, the former general Yang Jiong was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of Shazhou, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Inspector of Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang, former general Yang Jiong was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs in Shazhou, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Inspector of Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 集始入武興，以城降虜，氐人符幼孫起義攻之。

translations.literal: Jishi entered Wuxing and surrendered the city to the barbarians; the Di man Fu Yousun rose in righteous action to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi entered Wuxing and surrendered the city to the Wei; the Di leader Fu Yousun rose in revolt against him.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，氐、虜寇漢中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, Di and barbarians raided Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu, Di and Wei forces raided Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史蕭懿遣前氐王楊後起弟子元秀收合義兵，氐衆響應，斷虜運道。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Liangzhou Xiao Yi sent the former Di king Yang Houqi's younger brother's son Yuanxiu to gather righteous troops; Di hosts responded, cutting the barbarians' supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Xiao Yi sent Yuanxiu, nephew of the former Di king Yang Houqi, to gather loyal forces; Di tribes answered, cutting the enemy supply lines.

sentences.zh: 虜亦遣偽南梁州刺史仇池公楊靈珍據泥山以相拒格。

translations.literal: The barbarians also sent the false Inspector of Southern Liangzhou and Duke of Chouchi Yang Lingzhen to hold Nishan in mutual resistance.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei also sent the puppet Southern Liangzhou inspector and Duke of Chouchi Yang Lingzhen to hold Nishan against them.

sentences.zh: 元秀病死，符幼孫領其衆。

translations.literal: Yuanxiu died of illness; Fu Yousun led his host.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxiu died of illness, and Fu Yousun took command of his forces.

sentences.zh: 高宗詔曰：「仇池公楊元秀，氐王苗胤，乃心忠勇，醜虜凶逼，血誠彌厲，宣播朝威，招誘戎種，萬里齊契，響然歸從。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong's edict said: "Duke of Chouchi Yang Yuanxiu, seed and scion of the Di kings, his heart loyal and brave—when the ugly barbarians pressed with violence, his blood sincerity grew fiercer; he spread the court's majesty and enticed the frontier peoples; ten thousand li joined in covenant and answered in echoing submission."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong's edict read: "Duke of Chouchi Yang Yuanxiu, of the Di royal line, was loyal and brave at heart; when the enemy pressed him hard his devotion only grew; he spread the court's authority and rallied the frontier tribes, and peoples far and near answered his call."

sentences.zh: 誠效顯著，寔有可嘉。

translations.literal: His loyal achievement was manifest—truly there is what to praise.
translations.idiomatic: His loyal service was clear and truly praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 不幸殞喪，悽愴于懷。

translations.literal: Unfortunately he fell and died; grief wounds the heart.
translations.idiomatic: His untimely death fills us with grief.

sentences.zh: 夫死事加恩，陽秋明義。

translations.literal: For dying in service, grace is added; the Spring and Autumn Annals make righteousness clear.
translations.idiomatic: Those who die in service deserve added honor—the Spring and Autumn Annals make that righteousness plain.

sentences.zh: 宜追覃榮典，以弘勸獎。

translations.literal: It is fitting to extend posthumous glory and thereby magnify encouragement and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Let posthumous honors be granted to encourage such loyalty.

sentences.zh: 贈仇池公。

translations.literal: Grant the title Duke of Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him the posthumous title Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 持歸國。」

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff, return to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Grant him Bearer of the Staff and the privilege of returning to the state."

sentences.zh: 氐楊馥之聚義衆屯沮水關，城白馬北。

translations.literal: The Di Yang Fuzhi gathered righteous hosts and encamped at Jushui Pass, fortifying north of Baima.
translations.idiomatic: The Di leader Yang Fuzhi gathered loyal forces and encamped at Jushui Pass, building a fort north of Baima.

sentences.zh: 集始遣弟集朗率兵迎拒州軍於黃亘，戰大敗。

translations.literal: Jishi sent his younger brother Jilang to lead troops to meet and resist the provincial army at Huangxuan; they were greatly defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi sent his brother Jilang to meet the provincial army at Huangxuan and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 集始走下辯，馥之據武興。

translations.literal: Jishi fled down to Bian; Fuzhi seized Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi fled to Bian; Fuzhi took Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 虜軍尋退。

translations.literal: The barbarian army soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 馥之留弟昌之守武興，自引兵據仇池。

translations.literal: Fuzhi left his younger brother Changzhi to guard Wuxing and himself led troops to seize Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhi left his brother Changzhi to hold Wuxing and led his own forces to take Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「氐王楊馥之，世纂忠義，率厲部曲，樹績邊城，克殄姦醜。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Di King Yang Fuzhi, for generations inheriting loyalty and righteousness, leading and encouraging his following, planting achievement on the border, able to destroy the wicked and ugly."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Di King Yang Fuzhi has inherited loyalty for generations, led his followers well, won merit on the frontier, and destroyed the rebels."

sentences.zh: 復內稟朝律，外撫戎荒，款心式昭，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Again inwardly he received the court's laws, outwardly he soothed the barbarian wastes; his sincere heart was manifest—we greatly praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly he obeys the court's laws and outwardly he pacifies the frontier; his sincere heart is clear, and we commend him highly.

sentences.zh: 以爲持節、督北秦雍二州諸軍事、輔國將軍、平羌校尉、北秦州刺史、仇池公。」

translations.literal: He was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of the two provinces Northern Qin and Yong, General Who Assists the State, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Northern Qinzhou, and Duke of Chouchi."
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs in Northern Qin and Yong, General Who Assists the State, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Northern Qin, and Duke of Chouchi."

sentences.zh: 沙州刺史楊炅進號安西將軍。

translations.literal: Yang Jiong, Inspector of Shazhou, advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiong, inspector of Shazhou, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 三年，炅死，以炅子崇祖爲假節、督沙州軍事、征虜將軍、平羌校尉、沙州刺史、陰平王。

translations.literal: In the third year Jiong died; his son Chongzu was made Provisional Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs of Shazhou, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Shazhou, and King of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Jiong died; his son Chongzu was appointed Provisional Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs in Shazhou, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Shazhou, and King of Yinping.

sentences.zh: 四年，偽南梁州刺史楊靈珍與二弟婆羅、阿卜珍率部曲三萬餘人舉城歸附，送母及子雙健、阿皮於南鄭爲質。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the false Inspector of Southern Liangzhou Yang Lingzhen with his two younger brothers Poluo and Abuzhen led more than thirty thousand followers to surrender their city and submit; they sent his mother and sons Shuangjian and Api to Nanzheng as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the puppet Southern Liangzhou inspector Yang Lingzhen, with his brothers Poluo and Abuzhen, led more than thirty thousand followers in surrendering their city; they sent his mother and sons Shuangjian and Api to Nanzheng as hostages.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史陰廣宗遣中兵參軍王思考率衆救援，爲虜所得，婆羅、阿卜珍戰死。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Liangzhou Yin Guangzong sent the Central Army Aide Wang Sikao to lead a host to rescue; he was captured by the barbarians; Poluo and Abuzhen died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Yin Guangzong sent Central Army Aide Wang Sikao with troops to rescue them; the Wei captured him; Poluo and Abuzhen died in battle.

sentences.zh: 靈珍攻集始於武興，殺其二弟集同、集衆。

translations.literal: Lingzhen attacked Jishi at Wuxing and killed his two younger brothers Jitong and Jizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen attacked Jishi at Wuxing and killed his brothers Jitong and Jizhong.

sentences.zh: 集始窮急，請降。

translations.literal: Jishi, in extremity, requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi, desperate, asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 以靈珍爲持節、督隴右軍事、征虜將軍、北梁州刺史、仇池公、武都王。

translations.literal: Lingzhen was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Longyou military affairs, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Inspector of Northern Liangzhou, Duke of Chouchi, and King of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Longyou Military Affairs, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Inspector of Northern Liang, Duke of Chouchi, and King of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，復以集始爲使持節、督秦雍二州軍事、輔國將軍、平羌校尉、北秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan, Jishi was again made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs of the two provinces Qin and Yong, General Who Assists the State, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Inspector of Northern Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongyuan, Jishi was again appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs in Qin and Yong, General Who Assists the State, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Inspector of Northern Qin.

sentences.zh: 靈珍後爲虜所殺。

translations.literal: Lingzhen was later killed by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhen was later killed by the Wei.

sentences.zh: 自虜陷仇池以後，或得或失。

translations.literal: From the time the barbarians took Chouchi, it was sometimes held and sometimes lost.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei seized Chouchi, control passed back and forth.

sentences.zh: 宋以仇池爲郡，故以氐封焉。

translations.literal: Song made Chouchi a commandery, and therefore enfeoffed the Di there.
translations.idiomatic: Song made Chouchi a commandery and enfeoffed the Di accordingly.

sentences.zh: 機卒。

translations.literal: Qiang [text reads 機卒, corrupt].
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔曰：「行宕昌王梁彌頡，忠款內附，著績西服，宜加爵命，式隆蕃屏。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict said: "Acting King of Dangchang Liang Miqie, loyal and sincere in inner submission, achievements manifest in the western dress—titles should be added, to elevate the frontier screen."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict read: "Acting King of Dangchang Liang Miqie has loyally submitted and won merit on the western frontier; he should receive higher titles to strengthen the border."

sentences.zh: 可使持節、督河涼二州諸軍事、安西將軍、東羌校尉、河涼二州刺史、隴西公、宕昌王。

translations.literal: He may be Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of the two provinces He and Liang, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, Inspector of the two provinces He and Liang, Duke of Longxi, and King of Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs in He and Liang, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, Inspector of He and Liang, Duke of Longxi, and King of Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 」頡卒。

translations.literal: " Miqie died.
translations.idiomatic: Miqie died.

sentences.zh: 六年，以行宕昌王梁彌承爲使持節、督河涼二州諸軍事、安西將軍、東羌校尉、河涼二州刺史、宕昌王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Acting King of Dangchang Liang Micheng was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of the two provinces He and Liang, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, Inspector of the two provinces He and Liang, and King of Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Acting King of Dangchang Liang Micheng was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs in He and Liang, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, Inspector of He and Liang, and King of Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 使求軍儀及伎雜書，詔報曰：「知須軍儀等九種，竝非所愛。

translations.literal: His envoy requested military regalia and miscellaneous books of entertainments; the edict replied: "We know you need military regalia and nine other kinds—all are not what we favor sending."
translations.idiomatic: His envoy requested military regalia and books of entertainments; the court replied: "We know you need military regalia and nine other items—none of these are things we are willing to provide."

sentences.zh: 但軍器種甚多，致之未易。

translations.literal: But military implements are very numerous in kind, and sending them is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: Military equipment comes in many kinds and is not easy to send.

sentences.zh: 內伎不堪涉遠。

translations.literal: Palace entertainers cannot bear to travel far.
translations.idiomatic: Palace performers cannot endure a long journey.

sentences.zh: 祕閣圖書，例不外出。

translations.literal: Secret Archive books, by rule, do not go outside.
translations.idiomatic: Books from the Secret Archive are not lent outside by rule.

sentences.zh: 五經集注、論語，今特敕賜王各一部。

translations.literal: Collected Commentaries on the Five Classics and the Analects—now by special edict we bestow on the King one copy each."
translations.idiomatic: We grant you one copy each of the Collected Commentaries on the Five Classics and the Analects by special edict."

sentences.zh: 」俗重虎皮，以之送死，國中以爲貨。

translations.literal: " Their custom values tiger skins, using them for burial; within the state they are taken as currency.
translations.idiomatic: They value tiger skins highly and use them in funerals; within the realm they serve as currency.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：氐、胡獷盛，乘運迭起，秦、趙僭差，相係覆滅，餘類蠢蠢，被西疆而奄北際。

translations.literal: The historian says: Di and Hu were fierce and flourishing, riding the fortune of the age in succession; Qin and Zhao were presumptuous in rank, linked in overthrow and extinction; the remaining kinds stirred stupidly, spreading over the western marches and covering the northern bounds.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The Di and Hu grew fierce in their season; the states of Qin and Zhao rose in arrogance and fell in turn; the remnant tribes stirred on the western marches and pressed the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 芮芮地窮幽都，戎馬天隔。

translations.literal: Rouran land ends at the dark north; war horses are heaven-separated.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran reached the far north, their cavalry separated from China by heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 氐楊密邇，華、夷分民接境，侵犯漢、漾，浸逼狼狐，疆埸之心，窺望威德，梁部多難，於斯爲梗。

translations.literal: The Di Yang were close at hand; Chinese and barbarian peoples bordered each other; they encroached on Han and Yang, gradually pressed Lang and Hu, and the heart of the frontier looked toward imperial majesty and virtue—Liang province had many troubles, and here was the choke point.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang Di lay close by where Chinese and barbarians met; they encroached on Han and Yang and pressed toward Lang and Hu; the frontier looked to imperial virtue, and Liang province's troubles centered here.

sentences.zh: 殘羌遺種，際運肇昌，盡隴憑河，遠通南驛，據國稱蕃，竝受職命。

translations.literal: Surviving Qiang remnant seeds, at the juncture of fortune began to flourish, holding all Long and leaning on the river, far connecting to southern posts, holding states and styling themselves vassals—all received offices and commands.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang remnants seized their moment, held Longyou and the river routes, reached south along the courier roads, ruled as vassal states, and all received imperial commissions.

sentences.zh: 晉氏衰敗，中朝淪覆，滅餘四夷，庶雪戎禍，授以兵杖，升進軍麾，後代因仍，貪廣聲教，綏外懷遠，先名後實。

translations.literal: When the Jin house declined, the central court was overthrown; extinguishing the remaining four barbarians, they hoped to avenge the barbarian calamity; they were given weapons and staffs and advanced under military banners; later generations followed along, greedy to broaden fame and teaching, soothing the outer and cherishing the distant—first the name, afterward the substance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin fell and the central court collapsed, the hope was to crush the four barbarians and avenge frontier disasters; arms and banners were granted them; later dynasties carried on the policy, eager to extend civilization abroad—title first, substance after.

sentences.zh: 貿易有無，世開邊利，羽毛齒革，无損於我。

translations.literal: Trade in what exists and what does not, generation opening border profit—feathers, hides, and ivory, no harm to us.
translations.idiomatic: Trade in what each side lacked opened border profit—feathers, hides, and ivory cost us nothing.

sentences.zh: 若夫九種之事，有△△至於此也。

translations.literal: As for the affairs of the nine kinds, there is [lacuna] to this point.
translations.idiomatic: As for the affairs of the nine frontier peoples, [text lost] comes to this.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：芮芮、河南，同出胡種。

translations.literal: In praise: Rouran and Henan, together came forth from Hu stocks.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Rouran and Henan alike sprang from Hu stock.

sentences.zh: 稱王僭帝，擅彊專統。

translations.literal: They styled themselves kings and emperors presumptuously, monopolizing power in sole rule.
translations.idiomatic: They styled themselves kings and emperors and ruled by force alone.

sentences.zh: 氐、羌孽餘，散出河、隴。

translations.literal: Di and Qiang, evil remnants, scattered out from He and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Di and Qiang remnants scattered along the He and Long frontier.

sentences.zh: 來賔往叛，放命承宗。

translations.literal: Coming as guests, going as rebels, they threw off fate and inherited their lines.
translations.idiomatic: They came as guests and went as rebels, defying fate yet keeping their lines.

translations.idiomatic: Footnote 1.
